what_happened: The dispatch's decisive question (is [Finite F.WorldState] load-bearing at a call site?) resolved in three cheap probes: lean_references returned total=1 (declaration only), a repo-wide grep over *.lean found zero term applications, and a lean_run_code probe compiled the existing four-line proof at the binder-free signature with an identical axiom profile [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], matching the pinned #guard_msgs block. No Mathlib search tool was needed, so no rate limit was touched.

The declaration's own docstring (ShiftFiniteType.lean:159-160) justifies carrying [Finite W] while the module docstring (lines 38-43) argues the two-theorem split exists precisely so that only the finite-type half carries it. The signature edit therefore requires a docstring rewrite, and that rewrite lands under FormalSystem/ where no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md forbids 'no longer'/'previously'/'removed' phrasing -- the most likely way this task goes red on a gate unrelated to C16.

Planning was unusually cheap because the research round had already run the decisive probes: lean_references (total: 1) and a compiled binder-free proof probe with a matching axiom profile. The only plan-time verification needed was one lean_run_code call to confirm the ## Lean Challenge Statements block type-checks standalone (it must import the edited module's prerequisite, FormalSystem.Semantics.IntNormalFormEffective, rather than ShiftFiniteType itself, and re-declare Forbidden, to avoid colliding with the declaration it pins) -- exit 0, one 'declaration uses sorry' warning, no Lean build needed.

lean_references at the declaration name position returned total:2, not the total:1 recorded in reports/01_c16-unused-finite-instance.md. The extra hit is Tests/BimodalTest/Metalogic/EffectivePeriodicExtensionAxiomTest.lean:178, the '#print axioms' command, which names the declaration without applying it and supplies no instance arguments. The research conclusion (zero term-level call sites) is unaffected; only the reported count differed.

Phase 2's docstring restatement is net +1 line in FormalSystem/, which trips the repo's pre-commit typst-sync-check.sh Check 2 gate (formalsystem-line-count: committed=362642 live=362643) and blocked the phase-2 commit. The plan's Files-to-modify set names only FormalSystem/Semantics/ShiftFiniteType.lean, so the hook's own sanctioned remedy (regenerate typst/generated/status.typ via typst-sync-check.sh --fix) requires touching a generated file outside the planned scope. Phase 1's commit was unaffected because the signature edit was a 1-for-1 line replacement. Resolution: run the remedy rather than --no-verify, since this drift was caused by this task's own edit.

Second generated-metadata collision from the same net +1 line: check-module-invariants.sh FAIL INV reports README.md carrying a stale generated inventory block (line counts), so the aggregate gate exited 1 even though C16 -- the task's actual target -- reports PASS and every other group passes. Remedy is the gate's own printed command, 'bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory', which rewrites README.md: a second file outside the plan's Files-to-modify sets. Lesson for plan authoring: any net line-count change under FormalSystem/ drags typst/generated/status.typ and README.md's generated inventory block along with it; a plan that forbids touching files outside its declared set cannot land such an edit.
